_comment: GOLDEN VECTORS for the licence canonical-JSON contract. NOT hand-written.
Every signer_canonical_hex below was produced by RUNNING CM050's real
canonicaliseLicenseBody() -- the function the Cloudflare Worker signs with --
over the body in the same record. Regenerate with tests/fixtures/REGENERATE.md.
WHY THIS EXISTS: four implementations canonicalise licence bodies, each
carrying a comment asserting byte-identity with the others, and until this
fixture NOTHING pinned any pair. test_licence_gate.sh's positive control
mints AND verifies with the same rule, so it passes by construction and
would keep passing if the signer drifted.

provenance.generated_by: esbuild --bundle of the UNMODIFIED module, then node

known_divergence.summary: The SIGNER is the odd one out of four. license.ts:83 emits \u00XX for EVERY codepoint below 0x20; the other three emit JSON's short forms (\b \f \n \r \t) because that is what json.dumps does. Different bytes -> different Ed25519 payload -> rc=13 'signature did not verify', which reads to a customer as a bad licence rather than as our bug.
known_divergence.measured_population: all 32 codepoints 0x00-0x1F, each run through all three reachable implementations

reachable_today.why: stripe-webhook.ts:41 EMAIL_SHAPE_RE is /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/. JS \s covers 0x09/0x0a/0x0c/0x0d but NOT 0x08, so a backspace inside an email address passes validateEmail and is signed.
reachable_today.bound: Requires Stripe to deliver a customer_email containing 0x08. That is Stripe-side behaviour this fixture cannot and does not measure -- the claim here is only that OUR validator admits it.

known_divergence.fix_belongs_in: CM050 license.ts jsonEncodeString -- add the five short forms. The three verifiers are correct; the signer is wrong.
